text.insert: Board prioritization produces a deterministic candidate order and owns the capacity definitions used to fill an epoch. The
combines that ranked window with durable claims, cooldowns, exhaustion, and dispatch authority to decide admission and execution.

Ranking is graph-first: information gain, readiness, and reusable evidence outrank local closeness alone. A bounded closeness lane keeps targets ordered when graph evidence is unavailable or carries no useful information signal.
. Snapshotting does not run either build pipeline; regenerated artifacts become visible on the next read.

steps.text: Snapshotting does not run the build or objdiff pipeline.
Build one candidate for each imperfect function
Measure information gain, unlock potential, completion readiness, context quality, risk, and analog evidence
Use graph-first priority when information signals exist
Use bounded closeness ordering when graph evidence is unavailable or carries no information signal
Sort candidates and return the candidate window

rows: Candidate window
Ranked candidates inspected to satisfy admission.
At least the worker-pool target; may expand when fixed-epoch admission needs more candidates.
Epoch size
Total targets admitted to one epoch, as a fixed count or all schedulable targets in Full mode.
The admitted set stays fixed; priority refresh never injects out-of-epoch work.
Worker pool size
Worker jobs the Run Loop tries to keep active.
Consumer concurrency, not compiler parallelism.
Tool/build slots
Compile-heavy validation and tool operations allowed concurrently across epoch worktrees.
Independent of worker count.

text.insert: A run can admit a 256-target epoch, keep 64 worker jobs active, and scan a 512-target candidate window. Fast evidence refresh may reorder admitted-but-unclaimed targets, while the active target set remains fixed.

candidate_prior =
  information_priority_score
  + high_accuracy_bonus
  + accuracy_readiness_bonus
  + closeness_fallback_score
  + opseq_rerank_bonus

rows: Information gain, unlock potential, completion readiness, context quality, and risk.
Supplies the graph-first priority.
Capped log-compressed local closeness.
Adds a bounded finishability bonus; without graph data it carries the local closeness score.
Closeness combined with readiness and information gain, capped at 18.
Promotes nearly exact targets only when actionable evidence exists.
Raw closeness, fuzzy gap, and size, capped at 3.
Spreads the low-priority lane when graph data has no information signal.
Matched analog score and counts, capped at 48.
Applies only in opseq_hot_lane mode.

text.insert: A context-poor 99.x% target does not outrank a lower-fuzzy target likely to add reusable knowledge. Successful model reranking modes reorder deterministic candidates by p_win or p_match; scorer failure retains the deterministic order.

rows: Matched duplicate ref
A matched source shape can be adapted across unrelated files when assembly shape supports it.
Matched opseq analog
A strong already-matched assembly analog can place a target in the configured opseq hot lane.
Graph degree
A target connected to many similar functions can propagate more facts if solved or partially improved.
Linked incomplete functions
Sibling or connected imperfect functions can benefit from evidence discovered for this target.
Worker context quality
Nearby matched siblings, graph edges, or reducer facts make deep research more grounded.
Recent stalls
Repeated no-delta attempts cool a target unless new facts arrive.
Data/rodata risk
Header, static, section-order, split, and relocation-sensitive work needs slower validation and fewer parallel edits.

text.insert: A high prior is evidence of potential leverage, not authority to edit. The Run Loop admits, defers, cools down, or routes the ranked target under durable policy; workers receive only targets that have crossed that boundary.
